question: Should OpenClaw core expose this as prompt guidance only, or own a new authoritative output-governance security boundary with external validator execution?
rationale: The permanent boundary determines whether this is ordinary prompt configuration or a security-sensitive runtime subsystem; that choice affects configuration, tool authorization, streaming, delivery, retries, and operator trust and cannot be resolved as a mechanical repair.

options.title: Split guidance from enforcement
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped global guidance contribution first, while keeping actual tool and output enforcement in existing authorization seams or a separately designed subsystem.

options.title: Sponsor a core enforcement subsystem
options.body: Define and implement authoritative behavior across tool calls, streaming, final delivery, validator failure, secrets, retries, and every agent runtime before exposing the configuration.

options.title: Move optional compliance outside core
options.body: Use a plugin or deployment-owned wrapper if the requirement is environment-specific and no missing core extension API is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Split guidance from enforcement
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped global guidance contribution first, while keeping actual tool and output enforcement in existing authorization seams or a separately designed subsystem.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person most directly to canonical prompt assembly, bootstrap loading, and prompt-cache behavior affected by the decision.
